findings.title: enableSqlExpressions is dead, self-contradictory logic that ignores the feature flag
findings.body: `enableSqlExpressions` computes `enabled := !h.features.IsEnabledGlobally(featuremgmt.FlagSqlExpressions)`, then returns `false` in both the `if enabled` branch and the fall-through, so the function unconditionally returns `false` and the computed value (and the feature toggle itself) has no effect. The result is a function whose name says "enable" but which can never enable anything, a branch that can never do anything, and a feature-toggle read that is pure noise. If the intent is to hard-disable SQL expressions, this should be an explicit unconditional rejection (with a comment explaining the CVE-2024-9264 context); as written, the next person touching it cannot tell whether the double `return false` is deliberate or a typo, and static-analysis/dead-code linters are likely to flag it.

findings.title: Error text "sqlExpressions is not implemented" is misleading for users who enabled the toggle
findings.body: When a SQL expression query is received, the reader now always returns `fmt.Errorf("sqlExpressions is not implemented")`, even for operators who have explicitly enabled the still-existing `sqlExpressions` feature toggle. Those users will see a message implying the feature was never built rather than that it has been disabled for security reasons, which will generate support noise. The message should state that the feature is currently disabled (and the toggle has no effect), and the feature-toggle documentation/registry description should be updated to match, since the toggle is now inert.

findings.title: DuckDB-specific SQL string interpolation of user input left behind in dead code path
findings.body: `TablesList` still builds `SELECT json_serialize_sql('<rawSQL>')` by string-interpolating the user-supplied query after only a naive `strings.Replace(rawSQL, "'", "''", -1)`, and `tablesFromAST` still parses a DuckDB AST shape (`json_serialize_sql` output, `table_name` keys). This whole path is now dead because `RunCommands` is a stub that returns an error, but it is the exact code shape that led to CVE-2024-9264: if anyone later re-implements `DB.RunCommands`, the injection-prone interpolation is silently re-armed. Since the goal of the PR is to remove DuckDB, this parser (and the unused `DB.TablesList` method added in db.go) should be deleted rather than left as a trap. Note also `tablesFromAST` indexes `ast[0]` without a length check, so it would panic on an empty AST if it ever became reachable.

findings.title: No test asserts that SQL expressions are rejected
findings.body: This change disables SQL expressions in two places (the query reader in reader.go and the stubbed `sql.DB` methods here), but no test is added that asserts a `QueryTypeSQL` query is rejected by `ExpressionQueryReader.ReadQuery` or that `NewSQLCommand`/`SQLCommand.Execute` fail. Given this is a fix for a critical RCE/LFI (CVE-2024-9264), a regression test is important: without one, a future change that restores `DB.RunCommands`/`QueryFramesInto` or rewrites `enableSqlExpressions` can silently re-enable the vulnerable path with a green CI. Any existing tests that exercised `sql.TablesList` or SQL expression execution against DuckDB also need to be updated/removed, since they will now hit the "not implemented" stubs.
